links.note: The region around the Equator called the torrid zone because its climate is generally hot - this concept's word for it. Already linked and correct.

Why local time by longitude is inconvenient for a large country - this concept says it would not be convenient for a country to use many local times, and gives Russia with eleven zones and the USA with six as the cases where even one standard time is not enough.
Matching torrid, temperate and frigid to their latitudes and spotting torrid near the poles as false - this concept's latitude-and-climate sequence. Already linked and correct.
The part of a map that explains what the symbols represent - this concept is the symbols component, where map makers use a specific set of symbols so maps can be understood by a variety of users.
Social Science as the discipline that helps us understand our world and human societies - this concept's own summing-up sentence, that this is what Social Science is all about.

Naming a challenge of the 21st century - this concept lists them: rapid technological change, multiple wars and armed conflicts, rising social tensions, and the natural environment under great stress.
Social Science not being a science like physics or chemistry - this concept heads off that misunderstanding explicitly. Already linked and correct.
Naming a subdiscipline of Social Science - this concept lists geography, history, political science, economics, sociology, anthropology, archaeology and psychology.
Theme A, India and the World: Land and the People, covering the geographical world and the way to represent it on a map - this concept describes that theme.
Theme B, Tapestry of the Past, as the theme about who we are and where we come from - this concept says the past is a major source of our identities.
A map as a representation or drawing of some area - this concept's definition.
Scale as the ratio between map distance and ground distance - this concept introduces it as the first of the three components, each centimetre representing a certain distance on the ground.
North, south, east and west as the four cardinal directions - this concept's list. Already linked and correct.
Most maps simply having an arrow marked with the letter N - this concept's sentence on how direction is shown.
A globe defined as a sphere on which a map is drawn - this concept's definition, given right after the orange-peel demonstration.
The Equator at latitude 0 degrees by convention - this concept's statement. Already linked and correct.
Imaginary lines running east and west parallel to the Equator called parallels of latitude - this concept's definition. Already linked and correct.
The North Pole at 90 degrees North - this concept gives both poles' latitudes as 90N and 90S.

Why understanding human societies matters - this concept argues that to find answers to the fundamental questions and help build a better future, we first need to understand our world and human societies in particular.
How Social Science differs from physics - it uses scientific methods where possible but its focus, human society, is too diverse for set procedures and fixed results. Already linked and correct.

The aim of Theme C, Our Cultural Heritage and Knowledge Traditions - this concept states it, that every student should understand some of the cultural foundations of our civilisation and learn to appreciate their value.

Theme D, Governance and Democracy, and becoming responsible citizens - this concept sets out its questions about the political system, participation, rights and duties, and says the aim is to have a say in the policies that affect us all.
The purpose of a map's scale, relating a distance on the map to the distance on the ground - this concept explains it as what lets a huge place fit on a small piece of paper.
Crossing the International Date Line westward and adding a day, from Sunday to Monday - this concept's rule. Already linked and correct.

Social Science as the study that makes sense of the present for a better future - this concept frames it exactly that way, that we need to understand our world and human societies if we wish to help build a better future.

Multidisciplinarity - this concept is where the term is introduced, warning the reader to expect chess and ancient Tamil poetry in chapters on geography and festivals in chapters on economics, and saying that this is deliberate.
Ancient Indian astronomers and the madhya rekha through Ujjayini, which became the reference for calculations in all Indian astronomical texts. Already linked and correct.
The purpose and function of the International Date Line at approximately 180 degrees, opposite the Prime Meridian, and why the date changes across it. Already linked and correct.
Describing the torrid, temperate and frigid zones by latitude - this concept's connection between latitude and climate. Already linked and correct.
The past is still with us - this concept's own phrase, arguing that the past is the key to understanding the present and a major source of our identities. Already linked and correct.
The keyed sub-prompt asks what type of map shows mountain peaks and rivers in detail, which is this concept's physical map, and the 1 cm to 1 km calculation that follows is its scale.

A ship crossing the International Date Line eastward from Tokyo to San Francisco and adjusting the calendar date - this concept's rule and its placement of the +12 and -12 zones. Already linked and correct.

Students orienting a school map with north at the top, placing the library east and the playground north, and using symbols for buildings and trees - both the cardinal directions and the symbols come from this concept.
